title: Game of Life

content.problemStatement:
You're given a grid of cells where each cell is either 1 (live) or 0
(dead).

**Compute the next generation of the grid using Conway's rules, applied simultaneously to every cell based on its 8 neighbors (up, down, left, right, and the four diagonals), and return the grid after applying exactly one step.**

- a live cell with 2 or 3 live neighbors stays alive
- a live cell with fewer than 2 or more than 3 live neighbors dies
- a dead cell with exactly 3 live neighbors becomes alive
- every other cell stays as it is (dead stays dead)

Cells off the edge of the grid don't count as neighbors.
constraints: the update must reflect the state of all cells as of the previous generation, computed simultaneously
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: each cell's next state is computed from its live neighbor count in the original grid, all at once
the dead cell has 3 live neighbors so it becomes alive, and each live cell has 2 live neighbors so it survives
an all-dead grid stays dead, since no dead cell has exactly 3 live neighbors

hints: Can sorting the array simplify the problem, or does sorting take too long compared to a hash table lookup?
Consider two-pointer approaches if the array is sorted, or a sliding window if looking for contiguous subarrays.
Prefix sums or prefix XORs can answer range sum queries in O(1) time after O(N) preprocessing.
